name: BERTax taxonomic classification of genome fragments (Mock et al. 2022)
description: Superkingdom, phylum and genus assignment of 1,500-nt genome fragments, with every tool given the same reference or training data.

attributes.version: PNAS 2022, Table 1 and SI Tables S2 and S5
attributes.task: Assign a DNA fragment to its superkingdom, phylum or genus
attributes.source_locator: Results 'Comparison to Other Classification Approaches'; Materials and Methods 'Three Evaluation Datasets', 'Comparison to Other Tools'
attributes.scope_note: Architecture comparisons (SI Table S1), per-superkingdom AveP (S3), homology splits for BERTax only (S6) and ablations (S7) compare BERTax variants only and were not extracted. Figures and PR curves were not read.
limitations: Inputs are simulated 1,500-nt genome fragments, not sequencing reads or clinical specimens.
Database tools were given only the training partition as reference, not whole genomes; the authors call this a necessary deviation from their designed use.
Classification is at superkingdom, phylum and genus level, not species or strain.

attributes.source_locator: SI Appendix 'Details to PR-curve plots' (General Remarks; macro-average PR curves); Table 1 footnote; SI Table S2 caption
limitations: SI Tables S2 and S5 do not define the denominator of 'acc.'. Macro AveP counts samples a tool leaves unclassified as random guesses. BERTax and DeepMicrobes classify every sample and the database tools fewer, so AveP partly reflects how many samples each tool classifies.

name: Relevance of the BERTax closely related dataset protocol (Mock et al. 2022) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Machine-learning classifiers (BERTax, DeepMicrobes) and the baseline k-mer and alignment tools Kraken2 and minimap2 are scored on the same fragments with the same reference data. Tests whether a trained classifier matches reference-based tools when relatives are in the reference. It is proxy evidence: the inputs are simulated genome fragments, not specimen reads, and ranks stop at genus.

constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; inputs, references and taxonomic ranks differ between sources.
limitations: Simulated 1,500-nt genome fragments from RefSeq genomes; no sequencing errors, host DNA or clinical specimens.
Superkingdom, phylum and genus only; pathogen identification usually needs species or strain.
Database tools were given only the training partition as reference, not whole genomes, which the authors call a necessary deviation from their designed use.
